hints: Find the velocity at $t = 20\text{ s}$: $v(20) = 5 + 0.75(20) = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Since the particle decelerates uniformly to $v = 0$ at $t = 40\text{ s}$, the gradient of this line segment is $\frac{0 - 20}{40 - 20} = -1\text{ m s}^{-2}$, so at $t = 50\text{ s}$, $v(50) = -10\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Calculate the displacement up to $t = 50\text{ s}$ ($400\text{ m}$), then set the area of the return triangle $\frac{1}{2}(10)(T - 50)$ equal to $400$ to find $T$.
walkthrough:
Calculate velocity after the first stage ($t = 20\text{ s}$):
$$v(20) = 5 + 0.75(20) = 5 + 15 = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
The line segment decelerates from $v = 20$ at $t = 20$ to $v = 0$ at $t = 40$, giving a constant acceleration of $\frac{0 - 20}{40 - 20} = -1\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

Calculate the displacement from $t = 0$ to $t = 50\text{ s}$:
$$\text{Area above axis } (0 \le t \le 40): \frac{1}{2}(5 + 20)(20) + \frac{1}{2}(20)(20) = 250 + 200 = 450\text{ m}$$
$$\text{Area below axis } (40 \le t \le 50): \frac{1}{2}(10)(-10) = -50\text{ m}$$
$$\text{Displacement at } t = 50: s(50) = 450 - 50 = 400\text{ m}$$

The particle returns to O at time $T$, so the displacement from $t = 50$ to $T$ must equal $-400\text{ m}$:
$$\frac{1}{2}(-10)(T - 50) = -400 \implies -5(T - 50) = -400$$
$$T - 50 = 80 \implies T = 130\text{ s}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Velocity at $t = 20\text{ s}$.
Starting from $u = 5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ with acceleration $a = 0.75\text{ m s}^{-2}$ for $20\text{ s}$:
$$v(20) = 5 + 0.75(20) = 5 + 15 = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Step 2: Motion from $t = 20$ to $t = 50$.
The particle decelerates in a single straight line from $(20, 20)$ to $(40, 0)$. The gradient is:
$$\text{gradient} = \frac{0 - 20}{40 - 20} = -1\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
Extending this line segment to $t = 50\text{ s}$:
$$v(50) = 0 - 1(50 - 40) = -10\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Step 3: Total displacement at $t = 50\text{ s}$.
- Area 1 ($0 \le t \le 20$): Trapezium of height $20$ with parallel sides $5$ and $20$:
$$s_1 = \frac{5 + 20}{2} \times 20 = 250\text{ m}$$
- Area 2 ($20 \le t \le 40$): Triangle of base $20$ and height $20$:
$$s_2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 20 \times 20 = 200\text{ m}$$
- Area 3 ($40 \le t \le 50$): Triangle below the axis of base $10$ and height $-10$:
$$s_3 = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times (-10) = -50\text{ m}$$
Displacement from O at $t = 50$ is:
$$s(50) = 250 + 200 - 50 = 400\text{ m}$$

Step 4: Final stage from $t = 50$ to $t = T$.
The particle comes to rest at point O, meaning total displacement from $t = 0$ to $t = T$ is zero, so the displacement from $50$ to $T$ must be $-400\text{ m}$.
This stage is a triangle below the axis with base $(T - 50)$ and height $-10$:
$$\frac{1}{2}(T - 50)(-10) = -400$$
$$-5(T - 50) = -400$$
$$T - 50 = 80$$
$$T = 130\text{ s}$$

hints: The acceleration is the gradient of the velocity-time graph between $t = 50$ and $t = 130$.
At $t = 50\text{ s}$, velocity is $-10\text{ m s}^{-1}$; at $t = 130\text{ s}$, velocity is $0\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the gradient of the velocity-time graph from $t = 50\text{ s}$ to $t = 130\text{ s}$:
$$a = \frac{v(130) - v(50)}{130 - 50} = \frac{0 - (-10)}{80} = \frac{10}{80} = \frac{1}{8} = 0.125\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
teacher_walkthrough: The acceleration along a straight-line segment on a velocity-time graph equals the gradient $\frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}$.

Step 1: Identify the endpoints of the motion from $t = 50\text{ s}$ to $t = T = 130\text{ s}$:
- At $t = 50\text{ s}$: $v_1 = -10\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
- At $t = 130\text{ s}$: $v_2 = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Step 2: Evaluate the gradient:
$$a = \frac{v_2 - v_1}{t_2 - t_1} = \frac{0 - (-10)}{130 - 50} = \frac{10}{80} = \frac{1}{8} = 0.125\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
